subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a new hard 1 MiB public input limit, or should the memory-wiki owner choose a compatibility-preserving bounded-input design?
rationale: The existing CLI path accepted larger regular files, while the proposed fixed threshold is a user-visible behavior change rather than a purely mechanical resource-safety repair.

options.title: Preserve compatibility while bounding reads
options.body: Choose a bounded design that does not silently introduce a 1 MiB rejection for existing regular-file workflows, then add focused regression coverage.

options.title: Adopt the 1 MiB limit explicitly
options.body: Approve the new public limit, document the upgrade impact and error contract, and require proof for both accepted and rejected paths.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility while bounding reads
recommendation.body: Choose a bounded design that does not silently introduce a 1 MiB rejection for existing regular-file workflows, then add focused regression coverage.
